Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this is a multi-wake target-policy change; it requires inspecting the rollout keyframes before touching the controller. I’ll first read the workspace contract and the full skill instructions, then trace the assigned parent, sampled results, and inherited logs.

The contract confirms one editable policy file, and the visual-first skill requires comparing the best finite rollout with the most informative failure, including the shared prewarm sheet and metric/diagnostic cross-checks. I’m now identifying those cases and the inherited guidance lineage; I won’t edit the policy until the required diagnosis is recorded.

All four sampled solver results are exact deterministic replicas of the same successful 20.25° controller: capture at 244.547, mean distance 6.452L, and identical load/flow metrics. No sampled failure keyframe is present in this workspace, so I’ll use the strongest available successful sheet visually and use the inherited optimizer’s quantified 19° horizon miss / 21° rebound / naive-seed domain exit as the failure-side comparison, clearly distinguishing inherited textual evidence from current images.

The visual sheet and diagnostics agree on the remaining weakness: capture is reliable but follows a broad zig-zag with 4.293L maximum lateral target offset, while mean body velocity is only 0.0079L/time more upstream than local flow. Since amplitude, bearing sharpening, and posterior-lag changes are already bounded by negative evidence, I’m checking the allowed policy state for a bounded, body-frame corridor-retention signal that can damp wake-driven lateral excursions without changing the proven propulsion shell.

The visual-first skill now requires the diagnosis to be committed before the controller changes. I’m recording a one-axis phase-lead hypothesis: preserve the evaluated 20.25° propulsion shell and 0.30 steady bearing scale, but increase bounded bearing-rate lead from 0.25 to 0.35 so an already-correcting turn is eased earlier and a diverging bearing is corrected sooner. At the existing ±0.30 rate clamp, this adds at most 0.03 rad (1.72°) to the predicted-bearing term.

The required pre-edit diagnosis is now in place. I’m applying the single solver delta (`bearing_rate_lead = 0.35`) and materially revising the durable steering lesson to distinguish steady gain from steering timing: the inherited gain-sharpening failure says not to increase magnitude, while four exact current replicas make the residual lateral excursion a deterministic target for a one-axis lead test under this fixed prewarm.

The candidate and reusable lesson are updated. The workspace contract explicitly requires invoking the configured check-runner agent before completion, so I’m delegating only that bounded, non-CFD validation now; meanwhile I’ll audit the one-file solver boundary and parameter schema locally.
